Natural_Language: This part prescribes policies and procedures for assigning and performing contract administration and contract audit services.

Validation_Notes: Scope statement establishes the dual purpose of Part 42. Both administration and audit services are covered.

Natural_Language: Interagency agreements requirements for preventing duplicate oversight and ensuring payment for services.
Atomic_Propositions: P_42_001: Interagency agreement requirements consist of duplicate prevention and payment provisions
Validation_Notes: Parent proposition. Both subparts are mandatory requirements.

Natural_Language: Agencies must use interagency agreements to prevent duplicate audits, reviews, inspections, and examinations of contractors or subcontractors by more than one agency.
Atomic_Propositions: P_42_001_a_1: Agencies use interagency agreements; P_42_001_a_2: Interagency agreements prevent duplicate audits, reviews, inspections, and examinations of contractors or subcontractors by more than one agency
Validation_Notes: Mandatory requirement (must). Agencies are required to use interagency agreements as preventive measure against duplicative oversight.

Natural_Language: Subject to the fiscal regulations of the agencies and applicable interagency agreements, the requesting agency must pay the servicing agency for services rendered, in accordance with the Economy Act (31 U.S.C. 1535).
Atomic_Propositions: P_42_001_b_1: Fiscal regulations of agencies apply; P_42_001_b_2: Applicable interagency agreements apply; P_42_001_b_3: Requesting agency pays servicing agency for services rendered; P_42_001_b_4: Payment is in accordance with the Economy Act (31 U.S.C. 1535)
Validation_Notes: Conditional requirement: subject to fiscal regulations and interagency agreements, payment is mandatory. Uses material implication because payment obligation is triggered by the governing conditions. Economy Act citation is external statutory dependency.

Natural_Language: Cognizant Federal agency determination requirements.
Atomic_Propositions: P_42_002: Cognizant Federal agency requirements consist of determination criteria and continuity provisions
Validation_Notes: Parent proposition combining determination criteria and continuity advisory.

Natural_Language: The cognizant Federal agency is the agency with the largest dollar amount in negotiated contracts, including options, for each contractor business unit, except for educational institutions and nonprofits. The cognizant Federal agency for educational institutions (defined as institutions of higher education at 2 CFR part 200, subpart A, and 20 U.S.C. 1001) and nonprofit organizations (as defined in 2 CFR part 200), the cognizant Federal agency for indirect costs is determined by using the OMB Uniform Guidance at 2 CFR part 200, appendices III and IV, respectively.
Atomic_Propositions: P_42_002_a_1: Cognizant Federal agency is agency with largest dollar amount in negotiated contracts including options for each contractor business unit; P_42_002_a_2: Educational institutions and nonprofits are excepted from the general rule; P_42_002_a_3: For educational institutions and nonprofits, cognizance determined by OMB Uniform Guidance at 2 CFR part 200
Validation_Notes: Two-track determination: general rule for most contractors (largest dollar amount) and exception path for educational/nonprofit entities via OMB guidance. Material implication used for both conditional paths.

Natural_Language: Once a Federal agency assumes cognizance for a contractor, it should remain the cognizant Federal agency for at least 5 years to ensure continuity and ease of administration.
Atomic_Propositions: P_42_002_b_1: Federal agency assumes cognizance for a contractor; P_42_002_b_2: Agency remains cognizant for at least 5 years; P_42_002_b_3: Continuity and ease of administration are ensured
Validation_Notes: Advisory "should" indicates recommended practice, not mandatory. Five-year continuity is guidance, not binding. Flagged PENDING_REVIEW per advisory requirement protocol.

Validation_Notes: Parent proposition combining auditor responsibilities and agency designation.

Natural_Language: The auditor is responsible for analyzing contractor financial records, reviewing cost control systems, and performing other analyses requiring access to financial records.
Atomic_Propositions: P_42_101_a: Auditor responsibilities consist of financial analysis, cost control review, and other record-dependent analyses
Validation_Notes: Parent for auditor responsibilities. All three functions are concurrent duties.

Natural_Language: Analyzing contractor financial records or other related data and advising the requesting activity on the acceptability of the contractor's incurred and estimated costs.

Validation_Notes: Dual function: analysis and advisory. Both are required components of this responsibility.

Natural_Language: Reviewing the financial and accounting aspects of the contractor's cost control systems.
Atomic_Propositions: P_42_101_a_2: Auditor reviews financial and accounting aspects of contractor cost control systems
Validation_Notes: Single atomic requirement. No logical transformation needed.

Natural_Language: Performing other analyses and reviews that require access to the contractor's financial and accounting records supporting proposed and incurred costs.

Validation_Notes: Catch-all provision for additional audit functions. Access to records is prerequisite condition.

Natural_Language: Normally, the Defense Contract Audit Agency (DCAA) is the responsible Government audit agency. However, there may be instances where an agency other than DCAA desires cognizance of a particular contractor. In those instances, the two agencies must agree on the most efficient and economical approach to meet contract audit requirements. For educational institutions and nonprofit organizations, audit cognizance will be determined according to the provisions of the OMB Uniform Guidance at 2 CFR part 200.
Atomic_Propositions: P_42_101_b_1: DCAA is normally the responsible Government audit agency; P_42_101_b_2: Another agency desires cognizance of a particular contractor; P_42_101_b_3: Two agencies must agree on most efficient and economical approach; P_42_101_b_4: For educational institutions and nonprofits, audit cognizance determined per OMB Uniform Guidance at 2 CFR part 200
Validation_Notes: Default assignment to DCAA with conditional exception path when another agency seeks cognizance. Educational/nonprofit path follows OMB guidance. Material implication used for the exception condition.

Validation_Notes: Permissive authority ("may") to request services, but when requests are made, suspense date and information identification are mandatory ("must"). Conditional mandatory requirements triggered by the permissive act.

Natural_Language: The responsible audit agency may decline requests for services on a case-by-case basis if they lack adequate resources. Declinations must be in writing.

Validation_Notes: Permissive authority to decline ("may") conditional on inadequate resources. Tautology represents discretion. Writing requirement is mandatory when declination occurs.

Validation_Notes: Three mandatory requirements: maintenance, identification, and change reporting. All are ongoing obligations.

Natural_Language: To obtain the directory or information about audit offices, contact: Defense Contract Audit Agency, ATTN: CMO, Publications Officer, 8725 John J. Kingman Road, Suite 2135, Fort Belvoir, VA 22060-6219.

Validation_Notes: Informational provision. Contact details for directory access. No logical transformation needed.

Natural_Language: Perform the functions listed in 42.302(a) to the extent that they apply to the contract, except for the functions specifically withheld.

Natural_Language: Perform the functions listed in 42.302(b) only when and to the extent specifically authorized by the contracting officer.

Validation_Notes: Conditional: 42.302(b) functions performed only when specifically authorized. Authorization is necessary condition.

Atomic_Propositions: P_42_202: Contract administration assignment provisions
Validation_Notes: Parent proposition. All seven subsections are components of the assignment framework.

Natural_Language: The prime contractor is responsible for managing its subcontracts.
